core_obligations: Observe that it suffices to prove the third case, since the earlier cases are specialisations of it (proof lines 16173-16176).

Identify the high truncation of the complex with a shift of the top cohomology module and conclude from the module statement that it is pseudo-coherent in the relevant degree (proof lines 16176-16180).
Use the distinguished triangle of the two truncations and the cone statement to reduce to showing that the low truncation is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 16180-16186).
Choose a finite free module mapping onto the m-th cohomology of the low truncation, which witnesses its pseudo-coherence and finishes the proof (proof lines 16186-16192).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the third case (proof lines 16173-16176).
Use the truncation triangle to reduce to the low truncation (proof lines 16180-16186).
Construct the witness for the low truncation (proof lines 16186-16193).
difficulty_reason: The lemma turns finiteness conditions on the cohomology of a complex into pseudo-coherence at a degree, and the proof is a 21-line argument reducing the three cases to the third and then splitting the complex by a truncation. It identifies the high truncation with a shift of the top cohomology module, which is pseudo-coherent by the module statement, uses the distinguished triangle of the two truncations together with the cone statement for pseudo-coherence to reduce the question to the low truncation, and finally builds an explicit finite free module mapping onto the degree-m cohomology of that truncation, which is the witness required by the definition. Both reductions and the explicit witness are displayed.
